_meta.description: Live macro themes affecting currencies but not on the scheduled news calendar. Update as regime-changing events happen. Scanner reads this at brief generation time and displays it in the daily/weekly review.
_meta.howToUse: Each theme should include: (1) short title, (2) start date, (3) currency implications with brief reasoning, (4) a specific watchLevel that would invalidate the theme, (5) affectedPairs for scanner correlation. Retire themes by moving to _retired[] with an endDate.

themes.title: Japan-US joint FX intervention regime — USDJPY 155-160 range, BOJ September hike NOW LIVE, intervention credibility at critical test near 160
themes.summary: The intervention regime has entered its most acute credibility test as of Aug 14. USDJPY traded 159.14-159.43 on Aug 14, up roughly 150-170 pips from the Aug 10 open of 157.89 and now pressing against the 160 psychological trigger level. The pair has retraced nearly 60% of the intervention-induced drop from the 163.85 high to the 155.20 low. Two structural developments this week have materially changed the theme balance. First, the BOJ September hike is no longer 'off the table' — it is live. Reuters reported Aug 14, citing three sources familiar with BOJ thinking, that the Bank of Japan is set to raise rates as soon as September and could accelerate the pace of hikes from the current roughly twice-a-year cadence, with one source stating 'an early rate hike has come into sight' for the Sep 17-18 meeting. A Bloomberg report Aug 13 confirmed PM Takaichi's government is supportive of a near-term BOJ hike, likely September or October. MUFG's Lee Hardman noted Aug 13 that the yen 'has strengthened modestly overnight supported by building expectations for a faster pace of BoJ policy tightening.' Kyodo separately highlighted that the joint FX intervention was enabled by Governor Ueda's hawkish stance, suggesting the BOJ-MoF policy mix is now fully aligned. Second, the July US CPI print (released Aug 12) came in at +0.1% MoM and +3.4% YoY — in line with expectations and down from 3.5% in June — reducing the Sep Fed hike probability from approximately 54% to 40% per market pricing, narrowing the rate differential that has been the fundamental driver of USDJPY upside. July US PPI came in flat at 0.0% versus 0.2% consensus (Aug 14), reinforcing the softening inflation picture. The convergence of a live BOJ hike, a less hawkish Fed, and active intervention risk at 160 creates a three-layered headwind for USDJPY. The yen nonetheless remains pressured by wide interest rate differentials (Fed at 3.5-3.75% vs BOJ at 1%), fiscal concerns, and elevated energy/import costs per Trading Economics. Japan Q2 GDP arrives Aug 17 — a strong print would reinforce the BOJ September case materially. Recap of the regime: Japan deployed ¥11.73T in solo intervention Apr-May 2026 that ultimately failed; joint US-Japan intervention on Jul 30-31 (the first in nearly 30 years) with Fed NY selling euros for yen via Goldman and Morgan Stanley, confirmed via FIMA repo facility use; USDJPY post-intervention low 155.20 Aug 3; Bessent publicly endorsed further action and reiterated support Aug 7. The pair's drift from 155.20 back toward 160 in just 11 days without follow-up official action underlines that intervention is buying time, not reversing the fundamental dynamic — but the BOJ September hike, if delivered, would be the first genuine fundamental pillar under the yen since the regime began.

implications.JPY: MAXIMUM tailwind from three converging forces: (1) G2 intervention with FIMA repo and Bessent re-entry warning; (2) BOJ Sep hike now live per Reuters/Bloomberg, narrowing rate differential from the yen side; (3) Fed Sep hike odds falling to 40% post-CPI, narrowing it from the dollar side. Counter-risk: USDJPY at 159.43 is approaching 160 without follow-up intervention — if 160 breaks without official response, carry traders will interpret it as a regime shift. All JPY-cross short positions face maximum G2 + fundamental headwind. Sep 17-18 BOJ meeting is now a live JPY event risk.

EUR/USD hovering near 1.1450, GBP near 1.34-1.35, DXY near 100. USD most vulnerable into Jackson Hole (Aug 27-29) if Warsh fails to reassert hawkish credibility. themes.watchLevel: USDJPY 160.00 is the immediate critical level — a daily close above 160 without official response signals carry traders overpowering the regime; verbal intervention expected first. USDJPY below 157.50 = intervention credibility reasserting. USDJPY below 155.20 (post-intervention low) = regime decisively winning. Japan Q2 GDP Aug 17 — strong print reinforces BOJ September hike and is JPY-supportive. Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (Warsh keynote Aug 28) — dovish USD framing extends JPY-positive environment; hawkish framing partially restores rate differential drag on JPY. Next US CPI Sep 11.

themes.title: Warsh Fed — Jul CPI +3.4% in-line reduces Sep hike odds to 40%, Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 (13 days) is the live USD binary
themes.summary: The Warsh hawkish regime is under material pressure from two consecutive data misses — the Aug 7 NFP disaster (-23K vs +80K, -103K prior revisions) and now the July CPI report (Aug 12) which came in exactly in line at +0.1% MoM and +3.4% YoY, down from 3.5% in June. The in-line CPI print reduced the market-implied probability of a September Fed hike from approximately 54% to 40% per RoboForex analysis. The July PPI (Aug 14) came in flat at 0.0% vs 0.2% consensus, adding further disinflation signal. The energy component of CPI continues to fade: gasoline +24.6% YoY (down from 26.7% in June) as Iran war energy shock unwinds, with core CPI at +2.5% YoY and +0.2% MoM. Taken together, the last five days of data have materially reduced the urgency for a Sep Warsh hike without eliminating it — the Fed still holds at 3.5-3.75% with 9/18 members projecting at least one 2026 hike in the July 29 dots, and the 30-yr yield remains elevated. The Jackson Hole symposium (Aug 27-29) is now 13 days away and is the dominant USD binary event in the calendar. The official theme is 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy.' Warsh's keynote is Friday Aug 28. KPMG's August Economic Compass (Aug 11) framed Warsh's challenge as choosing between being 'prince or prisoner' — 'Jackson Hole is his chance to reset the narrative before the bond market does it for him.' With Sep hike odds at 40% and data softening, Warsh faces a credibility test: reaffirm anti-inflation resolve despite a weak labour market and moderating CPI (hawkish framing, restores USD bid), or acknowledge the dual-mandate tension (dovish framing, extends USD weakness). His Jul 29 press conference framing — 'a blank piece of paper,' 'step back from near-sighted debates,' 'big questions from a broader perspective' — suggests he will avoid explicit near-term rate guidance, but markets will force the issue. EUR/USD sits near 1.1450 per RoboForex, below the 2026 high of 1.1915, having pulled back from the post-NFP highs. The active scenario has shifted bearish per RoboForex technical analysis, with ECB at 2.40% vs Fed at 3.75% and US inflation still outpacing the eurozone. GBP/USD near 1.34-1.35. DXY near 100. The Sep 11 CPI print (covering August) is the next major data event after Jackson Hole. Sep FOMC Sep 16 is the hard policy event. Political dimension: Trump's critique of the Fed as obstructionist intensifies in a deteriorating labour market, creating additional Warsh communication constraints.

implications.USD: NEAR-TERM BEARISH confirmed by CPI + PPI misses reducing Sep hike odds to 40%. EUR/USD and GBP/USD at or near Q3 consensus targets already, suggesting two-way risk into JH. Jackson Hole is the critical inflection: hawkish framing restores USD carry bid 100-150 pips across board; dovish framing extends weakness toward Q3 upper targets. Structural hawkish argument (3 dissents at Jul FOMC, 9/18 dots project hike) remains intact but requires JH reaffirmation to re-engage.
implications.JPY: Rate differential headwind from Warsh narrative significantly reduced by NFP + CPI miss — do not fade JPY strength on carry differential alone. USDJPY bearish case now has three pillars: intervention, fading Fed hike odds, and live BOJ September hike.
implications.EUR: EUR/USD at ~1.1450, pulled back from 2026 high of 1.1915, technically bearish below EMA65/EMA200 per RoboForex. ECB-Fed differential still wide (ECB 2.40% vs Fed 3.75%). Warsh dovish at JH = EUR/USD retests 1.17+; Warsh hawkish = EUR/USD toward 1.1280 and opens 1.1080 target.
implications.GBP: GBP/USD near 1.34-1.35, essentially at Q3 consensus — two-way risk. BoE cutting limits GBP outperformance vs EUR. JH binary drives near-term direction.
implications.CAD: USD structural hawkish tailwind eroded further by CPI/PPI softness. Net: USDCAD primarily driven by Section 338 binary, with USD softness as a compressing background force.
implications.AUD: RBA on hold with easing bias. AUDUSD supported by USD softness. Watch 0.6500-0.6600 range.
implications.NZD: RBNZ same dynamic as RBA. NZDUSD benefits from broad USD softness into JH.
implications.CHF: SNB in easing mode; USDCHF under pressure, Q3 consensus ~0.80. CHF safe-haven bid in risk-off episodes.

themes.watchLevel: Jackson Hole Aug 27-29 — Warsh keynote Fri Aug 28 is primary binary: hawkish (hike still on table despite NFP/CPI) restores USD carry bid 100-150 pips across board; dovish or structural framing extends USD weakness. Sep hike odds currently 40% — a drop below 25% or rise above 65% before JH would be a major intra-period mover. Japan Q2 GDP Aug 17 is an indirect USD/JPY driver. Sep FOMC Sep 16 is the hard policy event. Sep 11 CPI (August) is next major data event post-JH. Sub-3.0% CPI reading at any point = dovish tolerance materialises, hawkish theme ends. 30-yr yield sustained above 5.5% = fiscal concerns dominate narrative. DXY closing and sustaining below 99.50 = market rejecting hawkish read entirely.

themes.title: Section 338 Canada tariffs effective Aug 19 — 5 days to binary, active talks ongoing but Washington recess complicates resolution, delay scenario emerging
themes.summary: The Section 338 binary is now 5 days away and the negotiating picture has evolved materially since the Aug 10 update. GHY International (updated Aug 13, citing the Globe and Mail Aug 12) confirmed that Canadian and US officials are in active discussions covering steel and aluminum quotas, retaliatory tariffs, alcohol shelf access, provincial procurement rules, and dairy quota allocation — a broader scope than purely Section 338 relief. Progress has reportedly been made, but the August recess in Washington is materially slowing the pace of talks, and a full resolution before August 19 is not guaranteed per GHY. GHY specifically noted that there are 'reasonable grounds to expect at least a delay to implementation while an interim agreement is finalized' — the delay scenario has emerged as a genuine alternative to the binary deal-or-tariffs outcome, introducing a third path (delay + ongoing talks) that would likely produce a modest CAD relief rally of 50-80 pips (less than a full deal, more than tariff-lands). The broader context has also clarified: MLT Aikins and Butzel Long legal analysis confirmed the US did not agree to renew USMCA in its current form, triggering new negotiations; US-Mexico USMCA talks have advanced more quickly while US-Canada have yet to formally initiate negotiations. Holland & Knight noted that Section 338(b) authorises the President to escalate to a full import ban if Canada maintains or increases its discrimination — an escalation tail risk markets have not fully priced. Carney 'stands ready to engage intensively' per Holland & Knight; USTR Greer confirmed talks have not been cut off. The Section 338 tariffs cover motor vehicles, alcohol, dairy, cement, furniture, fishing rods, seeds, clothing, and hockey sticks — three proclamations targeting autos, alcohol, and dairy separately. Energy products, potash, steel, aluminium, copper, autos/auto parts (already under Section 232), fish, and critical minerals are excluded. USDCAD dynamics: the pair has been compressed by the combination of intervention-driven USD weakness (NFP Aug 7, CPI Aug 12) and the active negotiation premium, trading in the 1.39-1.41 range. The 1.4080 resistance cap has held for consecutive weekly declines. With 5 days to go and a delay scenario now live, positioning is extremely binary-sensitive. Per Global Trade Alert, Canada's average US tariff rises 1.89 percentage points overnight to 6.27% if Section 338 lands as scheduled — a measurable structural headwind for the Canadian economy on top of existing Section 232 tariffs on steel, aluminium, autos, and lumber.

implications.CAD: ACUTE binary risk in 5 days. Three outcomes: (1) Full deal struck = sharp CAD relief 100-150 pips, retire theme; (2) Implementation delayed while negotiations continue = partial CAD relief 50-80 pips, theme evolves; (3) Tariffs land as scheduled = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, Canadian retaliation risk spikes. Washington August recess has reduced the probability of outcome (1) and increased the probability of outcomes (2) or (3). Reduce size, widen stops on all CAD crosses ahead of Aug 19.
implications.USD: Moderate tariff-narrative tailwind from USDCAD but offset by broad post-NFP/CPI USD weakness. Net: USDCAD consolidating 1.39-1.41 range rather than trending. Aug 19 binary outcome is the dominant near-term directional driver.
implications.MXN: Elevated secondary exposure — US-Mexico USMCA talks advancing faster than Canada per MLT Aikins, reducing Mexico's Section 338 risk but creating asymmetric CAD vs MXN exposure. USDMXN can telegraph CAD next-session in risk scenarios.
implications.EUR: Indirect — EU under 15% tariff ceiling from Jul 1; EU-Canada trade linkage adds modest contagion risk to EUR crosses in a CAD-shock scenario. EURCAD may be volatile around Aug 19.
implications.AUD: Indirect risk-off if CAD volatility spills into broader commodity bloc on Aug 19. AUDCAD may spike around the binary.
implications.NZD: Same as AUD. NZDCAD vol spike risk around Aug 19.

themes.watchLevel: Aug 19 12:01am ET is the primary hard binary — 5 days away. Three scenarios: (1) Deal struck pre-Aug 19 = CAD relief 100-150 pips, retire theme; (2) Delay to implementation announced = CAD relief 50-80 pips, theme evolves to 'extended negotiation'; (3) Tariffs land = USDCAD gaps higher 100-150 pips, retaliation risk activates. Washington August recess is actively slowing talks (GHY Aug 13). Section 338(b) escalation to full import ban is a tail risk if Canada formally retaliates. 1.4080 is key USDCAD technical ceiling — bulls need to reclaim it to signal tariff-risk pricing returning. USDCAD support at 1.3850-1.3900 on broad USD weakness. Section 338's permanent statutory nature means theme does not auto-expire on Aug 19 even if tariffs land — persists until explicitly revoked or superseded by a deal.
